name: Viktor Orbán
role: Prime minister of Hungary (1998–2002, 2010–2026); leader of Fidesz
summary: Leader of Fidesz and prime minister of Hungary. His governments have stressed national sovereignty, a family policy built on marriage between a man and a woman and on birth incentives, strict limits on migration, and close economic and diplomatic ties with China and Russia-linked energy projects. In a 2014 speech he described the state he was building as 'illiberal'; scholars describe the resulting system as a hybrid regime.

notes:
Views changed: as a young liberal and anti-communist founder of Fidesz (late 1980s to 1990s) he held positions that are not used here; answers reflect his positions from roughly 2010 to 2025. Two of his key speeches are covered only by secondary reporting: the 2014 Băile Tușnad speech (summarised in Wikipedia; the full English text was not reachable) and the 2022 Băile Tușnad remarks (Insight Hungary). Answers that rely on them are medium at most. Judgment calls: elite-replacement was answered +1 rather than +2 because he speaks of 'political forces' and 'people' rather than elites; discourage-race-mixing and diversity-weakens-cohesion were left null as nearby but not matching; restrict-foreign-funding and party-controls-media were set at +1 low because they rest on contested record evidence.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent research under the October 28 source-priority rules. No existing answers copied; no living-person inferences. The 2026 election observation documents substantial incumbent advantages, while the subsequent transfer of power prevents treating Hungary as a closed single-party state. Criticism of EU integration is not opposition to all international cooperation. Cross-border national solidarity is not a territorial annexation demand. Immigration and mixed-society rhetoric does not explicitly settle the separate proposition about interracial marriage and childbearing. Personal moral opposition to abortion is distinguished from his explicit 2022 support for retaining its broad legal framework. The original 2014 speech endpoint, current prime-minister site and original EUR-Lex judgments were unavailable; none is cited as read. Court findings below use the court’s own press account. The 2011 constitutional text is used only with his personal ownership of that constitutional project, not to attribute every clause.
